question.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall  the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
